You don't have to invest in Wisdom, you just get a benefit from any wisdom you DO have when you reach that level. Remember, you're *already* a Wizard. Any bonuses you get via subclasses are just gravy. However, it wouldn't be gamebreaking to make this intelligence dependent.

You could tie it to the channel divinity. Maybe make it wisdom times per long rest instead of one per short rest. And at higher levels it could become wisdom+x or wisdom*2.

You could also tie it into the amount of spells they can prepare. In older editions (and similar systems), the theurge had the big benefit of lots and lots of prepared spells. You could recreate this by letting the theurge prepare level+intelligence+wisdom amount of spells each day, compared to the normal level+intelligence. If you wanted to go even further with this you could also split the prepared spells. So a theurge can prepare level/2+intelligence wizard spells and level/2+wisdom cleric spells each day.

Emulating older editions is kind of the opposite of what we want to do with this current edition. I don't think we need to start adding in more math for no reason. This wizard isn't hurting for spells.
